solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: End of a lecture given prominence? It involves a mole

indicators.note: the final letter is pushed to the front, the most prominent place in the word

blocks.note: a lecture is a talk

explanation.surface: A teacher stressing the closing words of a talk, then a chemistry aside about moles.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of A TALK moves to the start. The definition only works because a mole here is the chemist's unit of amount, not the animal or the spy.
explanation.definitionFit: The katal is the SI unit of catalytic activity, measured as one mole of substrate converted per second.

clue.text: Bachelor in the UK damaged marriage contract

indicators.note: one part goes inside the other
a damaged thing is knocked out of its proper shape

blocks.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A British bachelor whose marriage agreement has fallen apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketubah is the Jewish marriage contract setting out the husband's duties to his wife.

clue.text: Such as magnolias nameless champion fed with running water

indicators.note: something fed with another takes it inside

blocks.note: anon is short for anonymous
an ace is an expert or champion
ea is a dialect word for a river or stream

explanation.surface: An unnamed prize-winning gardener watering magnolias.
explanation.walkthrough: EA is a Chambers dialect word for running water, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Annonaceae, the custard-apple family, belongs to the magnolia order, so its plants are classed alongside magnolias.

clue.text: Root-tuber pulled up round deserted plain

indicators.note: in a down light, pulling up means the word reads from bottom to top
going round something encloses it

blocks.note: the arnut or earth-nut is a plant with an edible tuber
D is the abbreviation for deserted

explanation.surface: Pulling up root vegetables on a bleak abandoned plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless Arctic plain with permanently frozen subsoil.

clue.text: Fellow leaving grilled fillets? Small one, as was

indicators.note: a letter that is leaving departs from the word
grilled food is cooked and changed, so the letters change order

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man walking away from grilled fish fillets, reminiscing about smaller portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fillets?' is also part of the definition: the setter means the architectural band, not fish. 'As was' marks the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A listel is a narrow flat moulding in architecture, an obsolete name for a small fillet.

clue.text: Piece of research stood out, penned by government administrator

indicators.note: letters that are out of place need rearranging
something penned by another is enclosed within it, like an animal in a pen

blocks.note: PC stands for Privy Counsellor, a member of the monarch's advisory council
taken as written

explanation.surface: A research paper that stood out, written up by a civil servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood out' reads as praise for the research, but 'out' is the shuffle signal acting on stood. The Privy Council is a body of senior advisers to the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives postdoc for postdoctoral research as well as for the person doing it, after completing a doctorate.

clue.text: Helper, a date out of sorts once crestfallen

indicators.note: out of sorts means disordered, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A helper feeling glum after a date went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the definition as archaic, a Shakespearean word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale-hearted is an old word for timid or dispirited, lacking courage, close to downcast.

clue.text: Spy sparse beard trimmed

indicators.note: a trimmed thing has had a part cut away

blocks.note: scrawny means thin and meagre
an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or other grain

explanation.surface: A spy with a thin, neatly clipped beard.
explanation.walkthrough: The beard is the botanical one, the bristle on grain. Scry here is Spenser's form of descry.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spenser, scry is a shortened descry, meaning to catch sight of or discern something far off.

clue.text: Racial, mostly mean after time

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the final letter goes
after places the next-mentioned word in front, with the earlier one following it

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ribald in its older sense means low or base

explanation.surface: Racist remarks that turned mostly nasty after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal relates to a tribe or ethnic group, so it can stand for racial in loose usage.

clue.text: What sharpens string, keeping tension in face

indicators.note: something keeping another holds it within

blocks.note: slang for a person's face
T is the abbreviation for tension

explanation.surface: A tense face while sharpening a length of string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharpens' is musical: raising a string's pitch by a semitone.
explanation.definitionFit: A dital is a key on a harp-lute that raises a string's pitch by a semitone.

clue.text: What sounds like understanding money

indicators.note: sounds like says the next word is matched by its pronunciation, not its spelling

blocks.note: sense means understanding

explanation.surface: Wondering which kind of money sounds like common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cents are the hundredth parts of a dollar or euro, so small coins or sums of money.

clue.text: Felony involving ethnicity, i.e. b––– racism in a way (9, two words)

indicators.note: arranged in a different way, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the two letters taken as written
the letter b with dashes, as a censored swear word is printed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Explaining a hate crime as 'bloody racism', with the swear word politely blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'i.e.' looks like a mere link but its two letters join b and racism in the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bias crime is the formal term for an offence motivated by prejudice against a victim's race or ethnic group.

clue.text: Party person with tons opening liquor store, we hear? He may not be trustworthy

indicators.note: one part opens another by going into it
we hear marks a word that is only matched by its sound

blocks.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
T is the abbreviation for tons
a wine cellar stores liquor

explanation.surface: A Conservative opening an off-licence with tons of stock, whose honesty is in doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: A storyteller in the second sense is a fibber, hence the hint of untrustworthiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller can be someone who tells lies, a fibber, as well as a narrator.

clue.text: Condition of healthy muscles – plenty observed round university

indicators.note: one word goes round another, surrounding it on both sides

blocks.note: tons means a great deal, plenty
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Plenty of fit muscles on display around a university campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonus is the medical name for the slight constant tension found in healthy resting muscle tissue.

clue.text: Sailor or his vessel – it's in the market

indicators.note: one word sits inside another, enclosed by it

blocks.note: taken as written
a tron is an old Scottish word for a public weighing machine and so the marketplace around it

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sailor or his boat is the thing for sale at market.
explanation.walkthrough: TRON is Scots for a market or the public scales that stood in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Triton is the Greek sea god, a seafarer of sorts, and also the large sea-snail shell he blew as a trumpet.

clue.text: Wavy? Soak, not fashionable

indicators.note: not means the following word is taken away from the rest

blocks.note: to inundate is to flood or drench
in means in fashion

explanation.surface: A wavy hairdo that you soak looks dated, not fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Undate, from Latin unda meaning a wave, describes a margin or line that rises and falls in waves.

clue.text: Boiler (9, two words)

blocks.note: the bare definition of the competition word
in a plain competition puzzle solvers write this clue themselves, so only a definition is printed

explanation.walkthrough: This was the competition word, in Azed's final competition puzzle: Azed gives only a definition, and entrants submit their own cryptic clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot for heating water to make a cuppa is a thing that boils, hence a boiler.

clue.text: Save page for Scottish cairn

blocks.note: bar means except, as in 'all bar one'
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Saving a page of a guidebook about a Scottish cairn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' is the preposition meaning except, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Barp is a Scots dialect word for a heap of stones raised as a burial mound or landmark.

clue.text: Spanish cash in property ownership, no small portion

indicators.note: no says the named bit is absent, so it comes out of the longer word

blocks.note: real estate is land and buildings owned as property
a tate is a small lock of hair or wool, a small portion

explanation.surface: Pesetas or euros invested in owning property, no small amount.
explanation.walkthrough: TATE is a Chambers word for a small tuft or portion. 'No small portion' reads as 'a large amount', but it orders the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Reales is a plural of real, an old Spanish silver coin worth a fraction of a peso.

clue.text: Treacly loaf made a mess of rubber raft (11, two words)

indicators.note: making a mess of something throws its parts into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sticky treacle loaf has made a mess on a rubber dinghy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carley float is a ship's emergency life raft, named after its inventor Horace Carley, often of inflatable or buoyant construction.

clue.text: Short tense argument? It may be petty

blocks.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense, a short form
a reason is an argument or ground

explanation.surface: A brief, tense row that could be dismissed as trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: Petty treason was an old English crime, such as a servant killing a master.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty treason was a historical offence of betraying a lesser superior, contrasted with high treason against the Crown.

clue.text: Try matting strip for coronary (11, two words)

blocks.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court
tat is a coarse cloth or matting woven in India
a tack is a narrow strip, as of land or cloth

explanation.surface: Trying to strip old matting brings on a heart attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Coronary is the everyday shortening of coronary thrombosis, a blockage in an artery to the heart muscle.

clue.text: Engineers put up with work on cylinder?

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
bore is the past tense of bear, to tolerate

explanation.surface: Engineers tolerated a job on an engine cylinder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' is one phrase meaning tolerated; RE is the British army's corps of Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebore an engine is to bore out its cylinders again to restore a true surface.

clue.text: Something for draining liquid boiling carrot

indicators.note: boiling stirs things up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Draining the water from boiled carrots.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture suggests a colander; the answer is a surgical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A trocar is a pointed surgical instrument in a tube, used to drain fluid from a body cavity.

clue.text: Dressing cutting gas in rocky outcrops

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes inside it

blocks.note: CS gas is tear gas
lint is soft fabric for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: Applying wound dressings after gas cuts among the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Clints are the flat limestone blocks of a pavement, or hard rock ledges in northern dialect.

clue.text: Following fashion, regret backing dullness of hue

indicators.note: going backwards means the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: a fad is a passing fashion
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Following fashion and regretting how dull the colours turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Fadeur is a French borrowing for insipidity or faded flatness, especially of colour.

clue.text: Central point's colt regarding pregnant mare?

indicators.note: a pregnant animal carries another inside her

blocks.note: a pregnant mare is in foal
C is the racing abbreviation for colt

explanation.surface: A young horse looking at an expectant mother at the centre of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: C sits 'in foal', just as a pregnant mare does.
explanation.definitionFit: Focal means relating to a focus, the central point where things converge.

clue.text: Energy imbibed in a tipple? It may be unattainable

indicators.note: something imbibed goes inside the drinker

blocks.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An energy boost from a nip of whisky, though the goal stays out of reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream as an ambition or ideal is often something hoped for but never reached.

clue.text: Eagle-eyed in part, causing mirth

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the hyphen

explanation.surface: Someone sharp-sighted spotting something funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is open delight or merriment, a close synonym of laughter-filled amusement.

clue.text: Gooey stuff surgeon cut from minor malfunction

indicators.note: cut from means removed out of the following word

blocks.note: a glitch is a small fault
CH abbreviates chirurgeon, an old word for surgeon

explanation.surface: A surgeon cutting out some gunk caused by a small technical fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Glit is a dialect word for slimy, sticky matter such as mucus.

clue.text: Young girl maybe, Dolores, full of what she's known for

indicators.note: something full of another holds it inside

blocks.note: Lola is a pet form of the Spanish name Dolores
it means sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A young girl named Dolores, famous for one thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Nabokov's heroine is Dolores Haze, so the whole clue also describes her; IT is the old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lolita is a sexually precocious young girl, after the title character of Nabokov's novel.

clue.text: Like W. Indian dish, cabbage, about swallowed

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the one that swallows it

blocks.note: cole is any cabbage plant
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A Caribbean recipe with cabbage that has been eaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: Creole cooking is the spicy mixed cuisine of the Caribbean and Louisiana, so a dish can be described as creole.

clue.text: Slopes, bare front to back

indicators.note: the leading letter is sent to the end of the word

blocks.note: scant means barely sufficient

explanation.surface: Bare ski slopes running from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: A cant is a tilt or inclined surface, so cants as a verb or plural noun means slopes.

clue.text: A journey in a container – such as ticks!

indicators.note: one phrase goes inside another, enclosed by it

blocks.note: a can is a container
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Ticks hitching a ride inside a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags that the whole clue is apt: ticks do travel on a ride inside a host.
explanation.definitionFit: Acaridean means belonging to the Acarida, the order of mites and ticks.

clue.text: Returning disease damaged tree Scots cripple

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so read backwards
a damaged thing is knocked out of its proper shape

blocks.note: mal is French for illness, as in mal de mer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recurring illness and a damaged tree leave a Scot lame.
explanation.definitionFit: Lameter is a Scots word for a lame person, built from lame with a noun ending.

clue.text: Pierre's love, including bit of sex given new life?

indicators.note: only a small bit, the opening letter, is taken
including means taking inside

blocks.note: rien is French for nothing, and love is nil in tennis
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's romance with a hint of sex brings him back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre stands for any Frenchman, so his word for nothing is French; love in tennis scoring is zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Risen means raised from the dead or revived, as in the risen Christ, so restored to life.
